text.content:
Netrunners who keep Pacifica alive. One part gang, one part government.

Turf: Pacifica: Coastview and West Wind Estate
Known for: Netrunning equipment and tech; the best hardware and ICE in the city; clean water, pirate power and a pirate net
Leadership: "Agwe", whom nobody has seen in person
Allies & rivals: Enemies: Barghest. Patrons of the Dirty Hippies; they watch, and recruit from, the Flickerheads
Hangouts: Batty's Hotel (#48), the Grand Imperial Mall's basement, the dead Pacifica Line stations

Not the posers of the 2020s, nor the old Voodoo Boys of Baron D, wiped out in the Purge. The tropical storm that devastated Haiti in 2062 sent a flood of refugees to Night City, most of whom ended up pouring concrete for the Pacifica resort. The district couldn't absorb them, went into a downward spiral, and the NUSA invasion during the Unification War supercharged it.

Since 2062 a man called Agwe, after the loa of the sea, has led a group of netrunners who organize the Haitian community. Pacifica started calling them the Voodoo Boys because they hide their identities from the locals they help; initiates know the group's true name. Agwe takes in anyone fleeing disaster or Barghest's reach.

In Coastview the Voodoo Boys provide clean water, pirate power, a pirate radio station and a pirate net that works better than Night Corp's did, and Pacifica keeps their secrets in return. They paint veve symbols where the cameras used to be and talk Haitian Creole on the comms. Their ICE is better than Night Corp's, and they sell the best netrunning hardware in the city, always asking what it's for.

What They Want

Whatever is behind the Blackwall. They keep asking where the old Old NET trunk lines run, and they pay well for the answer.

Edgerunner's Handbook p.26; Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.04, 06, 12
